proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, insulating oxyanion phosphate that is chemically compatible with both the LiCoO2 cathode and the Li6PS5Cl sulfide electrolyte. Its Li-rich, fully oxidized P(V) framework should resist oxidation near 4 V, and it is a well-known protective coating for this interface, so it is a strong first candidate for a low interfacial penalty.

LiCl is a wide-gap, electrochemically robust halide that shares the Cl anion with Li6PS5Cl. It has no P(V) oxyanion to oxidize the argyrodite sulfide, unlike Li3PO4, whose contact reaction released P2O5 and SO2. A halide coating should therefore give a smaller contact penalty while staying insulating and stable near 4 V.
